messages.subject: GGIR and VILPA
parts:
Hi all,

I now realise that the below discussion from April 2023 relates also to the recent work on VILPA (Vigorous intermittent, lifestyle physical activity) by Stamatakis and colleagues: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9800274/.

As people are asking me how to extract VILPA with GGIR, I have now tried to better understand what Stamatakis and colleagues did. No open-source licensed code has been shared in the paper that could clarify the calculation of VILPA, which is problematic as the paper comes with major claims about health benefits in a reputable journal without a clear definition of what is being measured! The promise that code will be send to UK Biobank does not make this paper reproducible as we need a direct link to the code for that.

Based on what I understand from the text, VILPA can only be calculated if participants report to never participate in planned exercises such as sport. In the absence of this self-reported information VILPA is reduced to just short lasting VPA that may or may not be part of scheduled exercise. It is less clear whether VPA that is part of an MVPA bouts is counted towards VPA or towards MVPA. The lack of reference to MVPA bouts in the paper gives the impression that MVPA bouts are not considered, by which time spent in VPA effectively reflects some of the time that we previously considered part of MVPA bouts. This would then also explain the strong association with health. The minimum length of 10 seconds is a result of the underlying method and does not seem to be motivated as an essential minimum length of VPA. In other words, using 5 second epochs would also seem justifiable.

As a result, VILPA may then be derived with GGIR in two possible ways depending on how you defined VILPA:
  • If we want to ignore short lasting VPA that is part of MVPA bouts then set the minimum bout length for MVPA at 1 or 2 minutes and look at unbouted VPA (GGIR part5 output variable "dur_day_VIG_unbt_min").
  • If we do NOT want to ignore short lasting VPA that is part of MVPA bouts then set the moderate threshold to a value that corresponds with vigorous and tell GGIR to extract 'MVPA' bouts lasting at least 1 or 2 minutes, which then will represent long VPA bouts (named MVPA in the variable name), and your unbouted VPA reflects short lasting VPA bouts regardless of being part in MVPA.

Note that GGIR has facilitated this for a long time, so from a methodological perspective there is nothing new here.

Best wishes,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

On Saturday, April 15th, 2023 at 3:03 PM, Vincent van Hees <v.va...@accelting.com> wrote:

Hi Jairo and Puchen,

If you set the mvpa threshold at a level that is indicative of vigorous activity then your MVPA bouts estimates will reflect vigorous activity bouts. If you additionally set the light activity threshold at moderate level, your LIPA bouts will reflect MPA bouts. The main challenge for you is to be aware of this new interpretation of the variable names.

However, this comes at the cost of LIPA being merged with inactivity.
To address that you could run GGIR separately with normal thresholds to extract the relative contribution of LIPA and inactivity and translate those to the analyses above. 

My proposal would be to first prove the scientific relevance of capturing all these bout  types via the approach I have described above before we consider adding this to GGIR.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

On Wednesday, April 12th, 2023 at 10:11 AM, Jairo Hidalgo Migueles <jairo.hidal...@gmail.com> wrote:

Dear Puchen Zhou,

Bout calculation for MPA and VPA separately are not available in GGIR for now. The only solution I can think of with the current GGIR version would be to trick the definition of the thresholds arguments so that you include two different thresholds for moderate physical activity (your moderate and your vigorous thresholds). You then would get two datasets for the part 5 in the results folder, one for each combination of thresholds. And you could use the MVPA information from the two datasets to derive the specific MPA and VPA thresholds. Not sure if this would work well as I have never tried this before.

Best,
Jairo

El viernes, 31 de marzo de 2023 a las 15:58:59 UTC+2, puchen zhou escribió:
Dear Vincent
I am writing to inquire about the calculation of moderate and vigorous physical activity (MPA and VPA) in different bout lengths. I have found that I am able to derive moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in different bout lengths, but not MPA and VPA. Furthermore, the value of unbouted and total MPA and VPA are not equal, which has led me to wonder whether there is a specific parameter I need to apply to obtain accurate MPA and VPA values with different bout durations.

Would you be able to provide me with guidance on how to calculate MPA and VPA using different bout lengths? Are there any specific parameters or adjustments I need to make to ensure accuracy in my calculations?

Thank you in advance for your assistance. I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Best regards,

Puchen Zhou
